rows.note: the lamp discovery found spot or point lights on the vessels in reach (the series craft carries lights); it counts lights that are off as well, so the rows lit_candidates and lights_off_candidates carry the switching
the start runs with Scatterer: RECON found the frame frozen with EVE present and Scatterer absent, so no frame or cloud row means anything in that set
control: with the craft's lights switched off (KSPActionGroup.Light false) no lamp is a lit candidate
with the lights switched on (KSPActionGroup.Light true) at least one lamp is a lit candidate by the module's rules (intensity, range, reach); the draw rows below count only these
control: in the forced snow with the lights off nothing is drawn, so snow_draws below is the lamps' doing
informative: the lights' state before the probe switched them (restored at the end)
interaction table (expected effects in .local/plans/atmospheres/D32-kw3b-spec.md): EVE loaded

interaction table: Deferred loaded. The shader of D32 is drawn by a command buffer with its own material and does not depend on RECON P8 (a foreign opaque lit shader under Deferred); Deferred's own lights are covered by lit_candidates and the draw rows with this mod present
interaction table: TUFX loaded (its bloom of the beam is a look item for E40)

clear air with the lamps lit (lit_candidates >= 1): no lamp is drawn (sigma below 1e-4, zero cost); if it fails, clear_air_sigma tells whether the body's real fog or haze is above the least sigma (then the air is not clear) or a source reads wrongly
clear air: no command buffer is attached on the flight camera (0 = false)
clear air: the medium at the first lamp is below the least sigma (informative: the fog of a clear day)
the test forcing of the field took the snow disc
the weather view reached a level of at least 0.25 in the forced snow
snow, all sources: at least one lamp is drawn
snow: the depth-copy and draw buffers are attached (1 = true)
snow: the depth copy was recorded in the 30 frames after the variant settled
informative: weatherCompose resolves to Scene (1 = Scene); it cannot fail while lamp.hostAllowed is false, so it carries no verdict
fog alone: sigma of the fog source at the first lamp, 1/m (ATMORESULT light_sigma_fog) (informative: it reads zero where the source is absent, so the row has no verdict beyond being present)
snow alone: sigma of the precipitation source at the first lamp, present in snow (ATMORESULT light_sigma_snow)

cloud alone with the test floor lamp.forceCloudDensity 0.8 (the cloud chain from density to sigma without flying into a cloud, which is not scripted): sigma of the cloud source at the first lamp, 1/m (ATMORESULT light_sigma_cloud), above the least sigma
cloud variant: sigma at the camera (inside the forced cloud), the term that dims the beam by exp(-sigma d)
informative: LampMath.CloudSigma at the forced density 0.8 with the default full sigma, to read light_sigma_cloud against (the body scale and cloud gain of the running game are applied on top)
dust alone: the body's constant haze at the first lamp, 1/m (informative: it reads zero where the source is absent, so the row has no verdict beyond being present)
the sum of the sources enabled by the variant, at the first lamp (informative: it reads zero where the source is absent, so the row has no verdict beyond being present)

the cloud density the lamp reads (volume pass and EVE layers) at the best of 64 places round the vessel, 0.5 to 4 km up; the real EVE layers at the sampled places; flying into a cloud is not scripted (the cloud rows use the forced floor), so zero only means the sampled places were clear
the sigma that density gives
the number of non-emissive EVE layers the lamp medium reads (0 without EVE)
the module's frame work, averaged (budget 0.05 ms; EVE's reflective sampling at 10 Hz is the part to watch)
player (series lamp): a lamp at sigma 0 records no draw (empty buffer)
player: the frame with the lamp at sigma 0 equals the frame without it
player: beam luminance rises with sigma over 0.002 to 0.05, each step above the one before
player: the mean over the beam's region against the CPU march of LampMath.BeamRadiance
player: the added light keeps the lamp's warm colour (red above blue)
player: a sigma of 0.08 at the camera dims the beam to at most 80 %
player: the glints raise the fine spread of the luma at least 1.5 times
player: atmoDebug contrib paints the beam blue (feature id 3)
player: a wall between camera and beam leaves at most 5 % of the open beam behind it
player: the Host composite against the Scene composite, relative difference of the added luminance (measured 1e-5 on 2026-11-11)
player: the Host picture correlates with the Scene picture over the beam's region with an off-centre occluder in front of it (measured 1.0)
player: the occluded beam is at most 90 % of the open beam, so that the depth clip is exercised (measured 0.867)
player: the scene's depth texture is bound at the end of the frame (the Host check is not run without it)

player (series lamp-time, exclusive): four lamps in snow at 2560x1440 add at most 0.5 ms of GPU time, judged on the upper 95 % bound of 8 alternating on/off differences (one set: run lamp-time of 2026-11-11 after the review fixes, third run of that day, mean 0.142 ms, bound 0.186 ms; the three runs of the day gave means of 0.107 to 0.189 ms and bounds of 0.186 to 0.288 ms, so the timer's run-to-run range is about 0.1 ms; the depth copy is included)
player (lamp-time): the spread of the on/off differences, so that the cost is read against the timer's own noise (0.052 ms in that run; 0.052 to 0.118 ms over the day's three runs)
player (lamp-time): sixteen lamps cost at least 0.15 ms more than none, so that the timer sees the lamps (1.207 ms in that run)

player (lamp-time): the full-resolution depth copy alone, without any lamp drawn, costs at most 0.3 ms on the upper 95 % bound of 8 alternating differences (0.0012 ms in the run of 2026-11-11; eight copies in one buffer 0.047 ms, so one copy is about 0.006 ms at the player's target); it runs every frame a lamp is drawn, so it is reported apart from the draws
player (lamp-time): the copy buffer was on the camera at BeforeForwardAlpha in every copy block, so that a low copy cost is a cheap copy and not a missing one
player (lamp-time): eight copies in one buffer cost more than none by at least 0.01 ms after taking off five spreads of the copy blocks' noise, so that the timer sees copies
player (lamp-time): the lamps add light to the 2560x1440 target, so that a low cost is a cheap draw

the temporal rows below are only meaningful under an upscaler: the lights start of K-W3b runs with DLSS (the lamp scatter is judged under DLSS first); the same start under FSR and XeSS is the E40 repeat
the temporal rows read the screen (the picture after the upscaler, interface hidden), not the camera's target (before it); 1 when the screen followed the scene in the liveness check
the beam exists at the converged frame of the turn test (scatter on minus off, mean luma over the eight beam points), so that the smear is a smear of something
the frame source delivered one frame per capture after the turn (frames between two captures), so that the figure below counts frames

frames after a 10 degree turn at 20 degrees per second until the beam's extra error against the converged frame is under a quarter of its own contribution (scatter on against off, same turn); at most 3 keeps the Scene composite, else Host (lamp.hostProven.<vendor> after the exposure rule exists). Name from the brief; the upscaler is the one of upscaler_name

ghost: the mean error of frames 4 to 10 after the turn at the beam points with the beam on, over the same without it (both plus a floor of a quarter of the beam's contribution), at most 1.2 (baseline + 20 %)

OPEN, decided by the replay and not by the probe: frame-generation duplicates with the beam on against off at most 1.2. Procedure in .local/plans/atmospheres/D32-kw3b-spec.md (proxy dump of the same turn with lightInMedium 1 and 0, tools/replay_fg.ps1, tools/replay_measure.py); the value is entered into the series table by hand after the replay

the lamp's copy of the scene depth (made at BeforeForwardAlpha by a shader pass) holds different values at nine places of the picture; a copy of one value is not a copy of a scene. Required: it can fail on the first K-W3b run (RECON P6 measured command-buffer taps, not a material that reads the global); wall_hidden_share is the check that the copy clips the beam
a frame source followed the scene (a white wall 4 m in front of the camera moved the luma at the centre by more than 0.03, target or screen); without it no frame row below has a value

at least 7 of the 8 points along the beam (15 % to 75 % of the reach, held to 40 m) are in the picture from the camera placement the probe found (distances 30 to 110 m, three pitches, eight headings, aimed from the axis of the drawn spot lamp whose axis is the most horizontal); the probe also fails itself (Check D32.beam_geometry) when no placement shows the beam

the elevation of the aimed-at lamp's axis above the horizontal (degrees); near 90 or -90 the beam is seen end-on, so the frame rows below measure nothing (the pad vessel's own lamps point at -88 degrees with a 3 m reach: the probe adds a horizontal spot lamp of its own, LampProbe.CreateTestLamp)
the side lamp the module draws and the probe aims at is the probe's own horizontal lamp and not one of the craft's down lights
informative: the length of beam the eight points span (the smallest of the lamp's range, 4 / sigma and 40 m), metres

forced snow, all sources, lamps lit: the mean luma the scatter adds at the eight beam points (scatter on minus off, three pairs, same pose and state). First thresholds of the series; E40 sets them with the look
the noise the beam is read against: mean difference of two scatter-off frames of the same state (the flakes move)

control (variant none, every source off, lamps lit, nothing drawn): the difference of scatter on and off is what the reading shows without any beam (flakes, light changes, the switch itself); the beam is read against it
beam_delta_snow over the larger of the control, the noise and a floor of 0.002: a beam that is not three times what no beam gives is not seen

inside the forced cloud (density floor 0.8 at the lamp and at the camera, precipitation source off): the mean luma the scatter adds at the beam points; in-game luminance in a cloud is measured here and only here (a real EVE cloud is not flown into)
the noise of the cloud variant's reading (two scatter-off frames)
the white wall (1.2 m ball, 3 m from the camera, on the line to the middle of the beam) covers at least 3 of the 8 beam points
the added luma at the covered points without the wall, so that a hidden beam is a beam that was there
the added luma at the covered points with the wall over the same without it: at most 30 % of the open beam shows through an opaque wall (the check that the depth copy clips the beam in the game)
the series craft has a crew and the IVA could be entered; when 0 the IVA hiding is unmeasured and the report says so
from inside the own vessel (IVA) no lamp of it is drawn (only emitted when the IVA was entered, hence not required)
